title: Peanut Butter, Vitamin and Mineral Fortified

content.title: About
content.content: Peanut butter fortified with vitamins and minerals is made from roasted peanuts to which a blend of micronutrients (vitamins B‑complex, vitamin E, iron, zinc, etc.) is added to boost its nutritional value. It has a smooth, creamy texture, a characteristic nutty flavor, and can be used as a spread, cooking ingredient, or dietary supplement.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fortified peanut butter is especially popular in the United States and Canada, where it is often included in school meals.
The added vitamins and minerals help meet a portion of daily micronutrient requirements, useful for children and people with limited diets.
Although commonly called a nut, peanut is actually a legume.
Unlike many commercial peanut butters, fortified versions are usually free of added sugars and trans‑fats.
Manufacturers often use micro‑encapsulation technology to preserve vitamin stability during storage.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: A serving provides about 7 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains heart‑healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats
items.content: These fats help maintain cardiovascular health and aid absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Fortified with B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B3 and B6 play key roles in energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Provides vitamin E and selenium
items.content: These antioxidants protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals: iron, zinc, magnesium
items.content: These minerals support immune function, blood formation, and muscle activity.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Individuals with peanut allergy may experience severe reactions, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Despite its benefits, the spread is calorie‑dense, so portion control is important.

items.title: Added salt
items.content: Some varieties contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Vitamin stability
items.content: Prolonged exposure to light and heat can degrade added vitamins; proper storage is essential.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use fortified peanut butter as a spread on bread, stir it into smoothies, oatmeal, or yogurt, and incorporate it into sauces and baked goods. For children, offer small amounts and monitor for any allergic reaction.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a tightly sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, store in the refrigerator and consume within 2–3 months. Discard if it develops a rancid odor.
